maturity: public fictional simulation/contract only; private implementation unassessed
question: Does a fictional issuer-signed identity and scenario-bound approval reject unauthorized changes before existing SQLite receipt insertion?
baseline: v0.3 caller-supplied principal and allowlist; v0.9 independent fictional sink integrity preserved
method: separate test-only HMAC-SHA256 identity and approval attestations; canonical JSON; scenario SHA-256 binding; existing v0.3 durable store

hosted.demo: executed and artifact upload step passed on both OS

conditions.keys: PUBLIC TEST-ONLY embedded fixtures; not real secrets

limits: Symmetric HMAC means verifier has signing key; no independent issuer trust.
Test issuer can mint arbitrary fictional subjects; no real login or human authentication.
Existing SQLite store returns idempotent replay; not a global exactly-once external-action guarantee.
Public deterministic test keys are not secrets and must never be deployed.
decision: retain draft, no maturity advancement, release or external action
next_experiment: Replace fixture issuer with isolated trusted IdP emulator and trusted clock, then adversarially test process crash, signed approval revocation, and measured blinded reviewer burden before considering real integration.
